requirements.sourceBehavior: Background subagent usage counts toward the session usage totals, as Cursor bills and lists every subagent run
requirements.evidence: S3 usage pools; Pi 1.1.0 getSessionStats() totals assistant usage, tool-result usage, compaction and branch-summary usage, and 'usage' entries (dist/core/agent-session.js); SessionManager.appendUsage writes those entries (dist/core/session-manager.d.ts), but ExtensionContext.sessionManager is ReadonlySessionManager, which omits it (dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts:223, session-manager.d.ts:178); the only caller is Pi's cache warmer
requirements.piMapping: none: usage stays in the child transcript and the notification details
requirements.gap: Pi 1.1.0 exposes no complete public way for an extension to add usage outside a tool result, a compaction draft, or a tree summary. Its 'usage' session entry would carry it, but ReadonlySessionManager omits appendUsage. A tool_result handler could attach pending usage to a later tool call, but that misattributes it and loses it when no tool call follows, so it was rejected (decisions.md D4). Foreground usage is counted (TASK-014); background usage is recorded in the child transcript and the notification's details.usage. Closes when Pi exposes a usage append to extensions.

requirements.sourceBehavior: A readonly subagent can still run shell commands that change no state, such as git log or git blame
requirements.evidence: S3 'no file edits, no state-changing shell commands'; round-2 parity review
requirements.piMapping: none: readonly children get no bash
requirements.gap: Pi has no read-only shell, and a command allowlist parsed by the port could be bypassed (pipes, substitutions, pagers), which would claim isolation Pi does not provide. The port withholds bash from readonly children. pstack's readonly workflows (how explorers and explainers, interrogate reviewers) only read code, and interrogate's parent runs git diff itself, so no pstack instruction needs it, but a readonly child cannot run git log or git blame as Cursor's can.
